paper_title: Multi-task head pose estimation in-the-wild
methodology: Paper Table 2, paper-native MNN result. MNN is a 9-stage residual U-Net-style encoder-decoder with lateral skip connections; its two 6DoF head-pose losses are attached to the 1×1 encoder bottleneck, while landmark heatmap and visibility losses are attached to the decoder. The selected Pre+Sym recipe first pre-trains landmark alignment, then jointly refines pose, alignment, and visibility. It is trained on 300W-LP only, using pose labels obtained with POSIT from the corrected 300W-LP landmarks cited as [50]; no additional training dataset is used. Adam starts at 1e-3 and halves after a 15-epoch plateau; training uses a 90/10 train-validation split, ±45° in-plane rotation, ±15% scaling, ±5% bounding-box translation, horizontal mirroring, HSV multipliers in [0.5,1.5], and synthetic rectangular occlusions. For AFLW2000-3D, the input RGB face is cropped from the rectangle enclosing the ground-truth annotated landmarks, enlarged by 30%, and resized to 256×256. The paper describes the complete 2,000-face set (yaw bins sum to 2,000) and reports no angle-range exclusion. Per-axis Euler MAE is yaw 3.34°, pitch 4.69°, roll 3.48°; mean MAE is 3.83°. Head-pose inference uses the encoder-only MNN (2,048,710 parameters; the full training encoder-decoder has 4,900,948).

The paper describes the full 15,677-frame BIWI set and reports no angle-range exclusion. Per-axis Euler MAE is yaw 3.98°, pitch 4.61°, roll 2.39°; mean MAE is 3.66°. Head-pose inference uses the encoder-only MNN (2,048,710 parameters; the full training encoder-decoder has 4,900,948).
